provenance_note: Consistency with METHOD + 3 external anchors. Expected pump flow, return and minimum temperatures, loop heat loss, pump pressure, annual cost, per-loop flow, return temperature and valve kv, the index loop and the sections below the minimum were computed by bench-src/ref/gen_plbcirc.py, an independent Python implementation written from the published method (_plb/circ/METHOD.md: DVGW W 553 proportional split, exponential pipe cooling with mixing of returns, thermostatic valve balance, Darcy-Weisbach/Colebrook, unbalanced network solved with scipy fsolve), not from the page code, so it checks consistency with METHOD rather than proving the method. Four external anchor cases (A1 single loop with the flow-pipe rule — return 51.44 °C, a hard fail; A1L the same loop sized to 5 K over the whole loop, DVGW W 553 preface / W 551 — 0.0122417 kg/s, return 55.0 °C; A2 W 553 two-riser split; A3 thermostatic loop) carry hand-calculated values typed in from a worked calculation with the standard formulas (EN ISO 12241 cylindrical layer, GEG Anlage 8, DVGW W 553 flow and split, exponential cooling); both the generator and the page are checked against them. Two invalid-input cases (bad_ins_*: insulation class outside none/geg50/geg100/custom, METHOD 8a) check that the engine refuses them with ins:<id> and the page shows no result; ins_missing_default checks that an omitted class means geg100. Pipe series (= plumbing-core MATERIALS) and GEG Anlage 8 thicknesses are input data.
